news.title: Messi drops massive retirement hint in emotional tribute to father
news.lede: Lionel Messi has shared a tribute to his late father, Jorge, on social media, opening up about how difficult it was to lead Argentina to the World Cup final and expressing uncertainty about whether he will continue playing football. “I don’t know what I’m going to do without you,” the post said in Spanish, shared on the footballer’s Instagram on Wednesday. news.title: Dad, I Still Can't Believe You're Gone: Messi's Heartbreaking Goodbye
news.lede: Lionel Messi has spent most of his life finding ways to express himself with a football. On Wednesday, he was searching for words to say goodbye to the man who had been there almost from the first kick. Jorge Messi, Lionel Messi's father, longtime agent, adviser and one of the central figures in his extraordinary football journey, died at a clinic in Rosario after a prolonged illness. For Messi, the grief is intertwined with one final football memory: the 2026 World Cup.

news.title: Messi says not certain to play ‘much longer’ after father’s death
news.lede: Argentina superstar and inspiration behind his country’s 2022 World Cup victory, Lionel Messi, said on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) he has “serious doubts” about continuing to play football for “much longer” after the death of his father Jorge Messi. “I don’t know what I’ll do without you, I don’t know how to go on. I just played football, and now I have serious doubts about continuing to do so for much longer,” Messi, 39, wrote in a message on social media after his father, who was also his agent, died last week aged 68. In the message, Messi, whose contract with Major League Soccer outfit Inter Miami runs till the end of the 2028 season, reflected on the final months of his father’s life, which coincided with the 2026 World Cup.

news.title: Lionel Messi has ‘quite a few doubts’ about football future after death of his father
news.lede: Messi’s father, ⁠Jorge, died last week at age of 68. Argentinian suggests he may not play on much longer. Lionel Messi has hinted that the end of his career may be near after ­admitting to “quite a few doubts” about his football future following the death of his father. Jorge Messi died last week at the age of 68 in Rosario, Argentina, after a long illness, with his health during this summer’s World Cup appearing to take a toll on Argentina’s 39-year-old captain.

news.title: 'I wanted to win another World Cup, I coudn't': Lionel Messi pens emotional post after father's demise
news.lede: For the first time since the death of his father Jorge Messi earlier this month, Lionel Messi has spoken publicly, sharing an emotional tribute that offered a deeply personal look at the grief he has been carrying throughout one of the most difficult periods of his life. The Argentina captain posted a photograph with his father alongside the simple caption, "Te amo, pa" ("I love you, Dad"), before accompanying it with a heartfelt letter reflecting on their relationship, the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and the uncertainty he now feels about life without the man who had been beside him since the very beginning." news.title: Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death
news.lede: Jorge Messi watched his son Lionel Messi lead Argentina to victory at the 2022 World Cup. Lionel Messi said he is unsure how much longer he will continue playing football as he posted an emotional tribute after his father's death. Messi's father Jorge was 68 when he died last week following a long illness. Jorge had been the Argentina forward's agent since he was 14 and watched him become one of the sport's greatest ever players.

news.title: Inter in advanced talks for Spurs full-back Spence
news.lede: Spence can play at right and left-back. Inter Milan are in advanced talks to sign Tottenham and England full-back Djed Spence, in a deal worth a minimum of £25.6m (30m euros). The 26-year-old has emerged as a key target for the Serie A champions, having enhanced his reputation at the World Cup, at which he made eight appearances. Despite coming under criticism early in the tournament, Spence ended up starting and impressing in England's World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina.
